text:
Dmitri: seeing apiserver leader flip across two masters in us-west-2 for the last 6m. etcd lease renews spiking, controller-manager queue growing, and GPU attach failures started around the same time.
Emma: logs show a bunch of `etcdserver: request timed out` and some 503s from the apiserver. cheap snapshot: 1) leader changes 2) request timeouts 3) controller backlog.
Carla: any recent infra changes in us-west? DNS TTL change or NAT gateway churn?
Ben: we pushed a route53 record update yesterday for the private controlplane VIP (lowered TTL). Not sure if that would cause leader flaps but worth noting.
Alice: GPU onboarding errors look like `AttachVolume failed for pod` with `rpc error: code = Unavailable`. That aligns with the time of leader flips.
devops-bot: deploy noticed: rollout/infra-controlplane-v3 tagged at 2026-03-20T02:01Z (by infra-ci). No immediate failures reported in canary.
Dmitri: hmm, canary passed but VIP DNS TTL drop might have exposed a race where kube-controller-manager attempts cloud calls while apiserver leadership is unstable. We should check controller leader election TTLs and cloud provider retry config.
Emma: grabbing logs from etcd-0/1/2:
```
Mar 20 02:10:12 etcd-1 etcd: rafthttp: rejected MsgApp (proposal dropped: ring buffer full)
Mar 20 02:10:14 etcd-2 etcd: timed out waiting for leader
Mar 20 02:10:15 apiserver: 503 GET /api/v1/pods (etcdserver: request timed out)
```
Carla: ring buffer full on rafthttp suggests IO or CPU pressure. NVMe IOPS in us-west have had a noisy neighbor earlier today. Are GPUs being attached causing iops spikes?
Ben: allocation logs show a provisioning burst — autoscaler spun up 18 GPU nodes within 3m for a training job. That likely saturated controlplane callers to the cloud API.
Alice: we also had a sudden increase in watch fanout because a batch of inference pods restarted at once (cache misses). apiserver watch handlers spiked.
Dmitri: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) roll back the route53 TTL change (raise TTL) 2) temporarily scale controlplane (add one ephemeral master) or move controller-manager to higher priority class 3) throttle GPU node onboarding (limit parallel attaches)
Emma: I can throttle autoscaler by setting `maxUnready` and `scaleUpDelay` in the autoscaler config, and reduce `burst` for the GPU nodegroup. Want me to apply now?
Ben: +1 apply the throttle. I'll also set a temporary quota on the cloud project for GPU attaches to 6 concurrent to slow the rush.
Carla: I'd rather also bump controller-manager lease durations to tolerate leader handoff noise: `--leader-elect-lease-duration=45s --leader-elect-renew-deadline=30s` (current is 15s/10s). Should reduce churn.
Alice: for the longer term we should: - add backpressure for attach calls in the attach controller - move heavy attach logic off the critical path - surface attach latency metric to the console.
Dmitri: ok Emma/Bob (Ben) do throttles now. Carla please prepare a config patch for the controller-manager flags. I'll coordinate a short maintenance window to add an ephemeral controlplane node if needed.
Emma: applied autoscaler throttle (kustomize patch pushed). command used:
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch cm cluster-autoscaler --patch '{"data":{"maxNodesTotal":"200","scaleUpDelay":"300s"}}'
```
Ben: cloud quota updated to 6 concurrent GPU attaches. Monitoring dashboards set an alert at 70% attach saturation.
Carla: PR opened for controller-manager flag bump: https://git.redwood/infra/ctrlmgr/pull/128. includes rollout plan and rollback steps.
Dmitri: after throttles, apiserver 503s fell from 8/s to ~1/s and leader flips stopped. etcd raft commit latency is trending down. Controller queue remains elevated but draining. Good first sign.
Alice: we still saw a handful of pods failing to attach; will run a sweep to reconcile failing pods and requeue their attach operations.
Emma: I'm leaving autoscaler limits in place for 1h, will revert if things look stable.
Ben: cost note — throttling will prolong job runtimes and bump transient cloud charges (longer instance hours). I'll add an estimate to the incident ticket.
Dmitri: +1 include cost delta. Postmortem action items: 1) add attach concurrency guard in autoscaler 2) add apiserver watch autoscaling and watchcache tuning doc 3) improve DNS change playbook 4) tune default leader election durations for controller-manager in cloud regions with noisy IO.
Carla: tagging @oncall and creating an incident with the above. Incident: INC-2026-03120-usw2-controlplane-attach.
Emma: thanks — keeping an eye for the next 30m. :thumbsup:
Ben: leaving notes for product teams running heavy GPU onboarding (heads up on quota changes).
Dmitri: good work. follow-ups in the incident ticket, we'll schedule a retro and decide permanent config changes. :coffee:
